ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the direct proportion function $y=kx$ ($k \neq 0$) intersects with the graph of the linear function $y=ax+b$ ($a \neq 0$) at point A(1, 1). What is the solution set of the inequality $kx \ge ax+b$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} When $x\ge 1$, the graph of $y=kx$ is above the graph of $y=ax+b$,\\
$\therefore kx\ge ax+b$,\\
which means the solution set for $kx\ge ax+b$ is: $x\ge \boxed{1}$.
